text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Debate in parliament ends in pandemonium. Ruling party Kenya African National Union (KANU) fails to push through amendments to the Public Investment Report.
- A Nairobi University student leader, kidnapped last Thursday, is found dumped in a church compound in Kiambu after he was allegedly tortured in police cells for five days.
- The Electoral Commission begins a three-month countrywide effort to realign its polling units in readiness for the registration of voters.
- Nairobi Mayor Dick Waweru announces that all contracts entered into with lawyers to collect rates on behalf of the council have been cancelled.
- The Central Bank of Kenya will issue floating bonds from 1997 as part of a wider measure aimed at containing prevailing high interest rates.
- Kenya Shell and BP Kenya reduce the pump price of their petrol by 30 cents a litre from Wednesday.
-Raila Odinga, FORD-Kenya faction leader, has decamped from Opposition party FORD-Kenya and is now national chairman of the Labour Party of Kenya.
